notes: Country determination: Germany (Hamburg) - certainty HIGH. Plan title block reads 'Neuengammer Hausdeich 256, Hamburg', German signage on balcony banners ('SAG JA ZU KLIMASCHUTZ', 'HAMBURGER ZUKUNFTSENTSCHEID'), German house number plaque '256', EN-style metal fence. Calc profile DE.

Building age: pre-1918 Gruenderzeit villa (decorative brick gables, rusticated render quoins, slate roof). Per DE rule, the historic front entry door (est. 2450 mm) is treated as [statistical] and cross-checked against Reichsformat brick coursing (~78 mm/course) and the plan storey chain.
Plan set: one sheet, Schnitt S-01 'Bestand', stated scale M 1:50, dated 28.08.2019, watermark 'Vorabzug' (preliminary). Sheet is read in normal orientation, no rotation.

The section carries a written VERTICAL chain only (0.20/3.15/0.20/3.40/0.20/2.10/0.20 m); no horizontal dimensions exist anywhere in the set, so building depth was taken graphically via the sheet scale derived from the vertical chain (GRAPHIC SCALE FALLBACK).

Section S-01 is interpreted as cut through the full-height gabled wing (walls rise to eave at top of the 3.15 m storey). The main roof body has a lower eave over a knee-wall band (red brick), visible in both photos.

Roof geometry: cross-gable - transverse gabled wing (front-right / rear-left as seen from street) intersecting a main roof that is hipped at the left end (seen from street). building.roof_type set to 'other' with this note.
Sloped dike site: grade at the rear is approx. 300-500 mm lower than at the street side; rear entry reached over ~8 exterior steps. Datum = grade at front (street) side.
Large tree partially occludes the front-left facade (photo 2) and the rear-left gable (photo 1); far-left front window only partially visible.
Facade corners of photo 2 lie near the image frame edges; possible wide-angle compression at the far-left window position.

warnings: Depth basis oblique_only: no frontal left/right side photo exists; footprint depth capped at confidence low.

Graphic scale fallback used for building depth: section S-01 carries only a vertical written chain; horizontal extent measured graphically via the 1:50 sheet scale derived from the 9450 mm vertical chain.

Plan vs. photo: section S-01 shows full-height (3.15 m) upper-storey walls to the eave, while photos show the main roof springing from a lower knee-wall band (~6.1 m eave). Section interpreted as cut through the full-height gabled wing; main-roof eave (6100 mm) taken from photos, wing eave (7950 mm) from the plan chain.
Openings likely undercounted on left and right elevations: no photos exist of those sides; left/right walls emitted with no openings.
Historic front entry door used as a scale is statistical per DE pre-1950 rule (assumed 2450 mm); implied door height from brick-coursing chain ~2400-2550 mm, consistent within tolerance.
Ground line at the rear elevation is partially occluded (wood pile, barrels); rear grade offset assumed -300 mm; rear height confidences capped at medium.
Bay window W-4 sits on the projecting bay (AT-3), i.e. ~1200 mm in front of the main facade plane; it is nevertheless subtracted from WL-1 net area for simplicity.
Front facade corners lie near the photo 2 frame edges; W-1 position/size may be affected by wide-angle compression.

Roof-facet areas and valley/hip lengths are derived from an estimated cross-gable model (width 12500 x depth 11000, main pitch ~41 deg, wing pitch ~45 deg) and are mutually consistent but individually low confidence.
